div.p: Located in Leicester Street from the 1910s to the late 1940s.

In the 1930s, the business at 100 Leicester Street supplied bent timber for a wide range of uses including caravans, surf boards, and trotting sulky shafts. In 1941 the site was offered for sale as part of the estate of the late John Petersen. In 1949, a large fire destroyed part of the building including the boiler room, office, and coach building section, and it seems the business did not recover. Frederick Clelland Casey was acquitted of arson, though he had earlier and later convictions for similar offences. A 1954 photograph shows the demolition of a 100-year-old chimney on the site.
